Magical gene / lines and strokes

Qhada

Broad ribbons of colour draped along the topline with speckling filling the gaps between them, and hair-thin stripes of the same colours through the mane and tail.

What it does

QhadaLarge stripes run along the neck, back and hindquarters, following the body's curve so they look draped rather than drawn - five to twelve inches across, layered with one colour leading and another behind it. The spaces between them are not empty: speckling fills them, denser than the horse's ordinary speckling. The mane and tail carry the same colours as hair-thin stripes, in deliberate contrast to the ribbons, and there is no regular striping. White patterns are allowed and pass underneath. The hooves take a speckling colour, and there is no pupil.
Wild typeNo ribbons.

What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 1,250 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/qhada.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.qhada
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority374 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order
AllelesQha · n
Varies per horse4 values drawn once off the expressing allele copy, so a foal that inherits the copy inherits the look
Built fromAXIS, SPECKLE, STROKES, TOWARD

What it paints

Qhada

  1. the leading ribbon along the topline — STROKES × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  2. the second ribbon behind it — STROKES × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  3. speckling in the gaps between them — SPECKLE × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  4. hair-thin stripes through the mane and tail — STROKES, painted with TOWARD
  5. hooves in a speckling colour — AXIS, painted with TOWARD
